plan.analysis: Choose N=3: the measured, correct baseline and source reveal three complementary opportunities—its generic r,c,k loop reads B with a stride, it has no explicit SIMD kernel, and it does not use the supplied OpenMP/thread budget. Separate trees can explore locality, arithmetic throughput, and thread scaling without making all three pursue the same mechanism. The provided baseline search has three samples (mean 0.143570912 s, score 0.5) and is marked correct; there is no independent confirmation or per-size/thread breakdown, so treat it as a reference rather than evidence for any particular speedup. Preserve generic behavior for every valid size, signed inputs, full output overwrite, tolerance, and thread budget. The available time supports three concurrent investigations while leaving time for integration and independent confirmation.

children.objective: Improve single-thread memory locality for arbitrary valid n. As a low-cost control, compare scalar i-k-j loop interchange against cache-level blocking and/or per-call B-panel packing; measure packing, scratch allocation, and output initialization as part of the complete call. Keep the main comparison focused on memory locality rather than explicit SIMD or OpenMP, and report any useful hybrid separately. Handle edge tiles, validate correctness including complete C overwrite, and compare repeated timings.
children.subject: Cache blocking and B locality

children.objective: Improve single-thread arithmetic throughput with a register-blocked, vectorizable or target-supported SIMD microkernel, such as an outer-product kernel that reuses input values across output elements. Handle arbitrary dimensions and tails, signed values, and numerical tolerance. Keep the focus on the compute kernel rather than OpenMP or full-panel packing; measure the actual target build and validate correctness.
children.subject: SIMD and register microkernel

children.objective: Explore OpenMP decomposition and scheduling over disjoint output rows or tiles, explicitly respecting the run-time threads argument as an upper bound and avoiding races or oversubscription. For a controlled comparison, use the same arithmetic kernel in serial and parallel configurations where practical; report 1- and 4-thread results, including OpenMP and output-initialization costs, and avoid clearing C twice or excluding initialization from timing. Preserve generic dimensions and complete output overwrite, and validate correctness.
children.subject: OpenMP thread-budget scaling
